rationale: Both are short and correct. A stores the roster in a single name-to-grade dictionary, so there is one source of truth: duplicate detection is a direct membership test, and roster and grade are simple sorted views of that data. B keeps two structures that must stay in sync, a grade-to-names mapping and a separate enrolled set. That is redundant state that adds a little risk. B does make the per-grade lookup and the roster comprehension slightly more natural, and it returns a bool from add_student, which nothing uses. Both return the internal _added list directly. A's simpler data model is the better trade-off.
